result.rationale: The server schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.object({bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email())})` has no uniqueness refine, while the client's ZAddGuestsInputSchema does (`uniqueEmails.size === emails.length`). The handler's `uniqueGuests` filter only removes emails already present in `booking.attendees`, not duplicates within the request, so `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` would pass validation and `createMany` would insert two identical rows. Mechanism fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: The server-side schema lacks the uniqueness refine the client enforces in AddGuestsDialog (parallel client+server validation that has already drifted in this same diff), so duplicate emails within one request pass server validation and are all inserted by createMany. Any non-UI caller (API consumer) submits `guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` and gets two identical attendee rows for one booking; the uniqueness invariant exists only in the discarded client copy.
